name: claude-orchestrator
description: VS Code extension to orchestrate multiple Claude Code agents in parallel via embedded MCP server + observable kanban dashboard.

commands.title: Claude Orchestrator: Rescan projects and sessions
Claude Orchestrator: Register MCP in Claude Code
Claude Orchestrator: Inject MCP directive into workspaces
Claude Orchestrator: Install global activity hooks
Claude Orchestrator: Uninstall global activity hooks

claudeOrchestrator.projectsRoot.description: Absolute paths. Each direct subfolder of a path here is treated as a project. Used to derive project/task labels in the dashboard from the agent cwd. Tildes (~) are expanded to the user home.

claudeOrchestrator.scannerRefreshSec.description: Auto-refresh interval (seconds) for the project + session scanner. 0 disables auto-refresh (default) — use the 'Rescan' button in the dashboard toolbar or the 'Rescan projects and sessions' command. Re-scanning re-parses every .jsonl from disk; with many projects (50+) keep this at 0 to avoid recurring I/O spikes.

claudeOrchestrator.resumeConfirm.description: If true, show a confirmation dialog before resuming a past Claude session.

claudeOrchestrator.cancelConfirm.description: If true, show a confirmation dialog before cancelling a running agent from the dashboard.

claudeOrchestrator.notifyOnComplete.description: If true, show a VS Code notification toast when an agent finishes (done / failed / cancelled). Click 'Open detail' on the toast to jump to the detail panel.

enumDescriptions: Opus — highest capability, slowest, most expensive
claudeOrchestrator.defaultModel.description: Default Claude model used when an agent is spawned without an explicit model. Applies to MCP spawn_agents calls that omit the 'model' field and to the palette command 'Test Agent' when the user picks the default option.

claudeOrchestrator.maxAgentRuntimeSec.description: Tiempo máximo (en segundos) que un agente puede estar vivo. Pasado ese tiempo, el bridge lo cancela automáticamente con status=failed y reason=max_runtime_exceeded. Cap defensivo contra agentes pegados. Subí este número para tareas largas (migraciones, audits completos). Default: 2000 (~33 min).

claudeOrchestrator.stuckDetectionSec.description: Si un agente running no emite ningún evento durante N segundos, wait_for_agents lo marca con suspected_stuck=true en la respuesta (NO lo cancela — el chat decide). Subí este número si tus tareas legítimamente quedan en silencio más tiempo entre eventos (Read de archivos grandes, Bash silenciosos). Default: 60s.

claudeOrchestrator.autoRegisterMcp.description: If true (default), the extension writes its MCP server entry directly into ~/.claude.json on activation, so the user does not need to run `claude mcp add-json` manually. Set to false to opt out and use the manual setup command printed to the output channel.

claudeOrchestrator.autoInjectClaudeMd.description: If true (default), the extension injects a marked section into every CLAUDE.md it finds in the direct subfolders of `claudeOrchestrator.projectsRoot`. The section tells the chat caller to prefer `spawn_agents` over Bash/Task for this workspace, making natural-language prompts ('lanza 3 agentes paralelos') work without explicit tool naming. Only updates existing CLAUDE.md files — never creates new ones automatically (use the `Inject MCP directive into workspaces` palette command for that).

claudeOrchestrator.ingesterDebug.description: Experimental (read-only activity viewer): tail the global hook event stream written by 'Install global activity hooks' and log the translated agent events to the output channel. Scaffolding while the viewer is wired to the dashboard; has no effect on the orchestrator.

claudeOrchestrator.showTransportState.description: If true, show a yellow banner at the top of the dashboard when a wait_for_agents call has been blocked for >60s without resolving (heuristic for a degraded MCP transport — agents continue running but the chat caller never got the long-poll response). Off by default until validated in productive use; flip to true to opt in.

enumDescriptions: Open the resumed session in the Claude Code sidebar chat (requires the 'anthropic.claude-code' extension). Falls back to terminal if the extension is missing.
Open the resumed session in a new VS Code terminal running 'claude --resume <id>'.
claudeOrchestrator.resumeIn.description: Where to open a past session when clicking Resume. 'chat' uses the Claude Code extension's URI handler; 'terminal' spawns a new VS Code terminal.

enumDescriptions: Legacy: no extra verification. wait_for_agents returns the agent's free-text last_message as-is. Use only for atomic tasks where the structured exit adds noise.

Mechanism D only (default). The orchestrator appends an exit-report instruction to every prompt and parses the agent's final JSON block. Auto-promotes status to 'needs_review' when the agent declares decisions_made_without_consultation or uncertainties. Zero runtime cost — only changes the agent's prompt.

Mechanism A only. After wait_for_agents, the orchestrator spawns a Haiku critic per terminal agent that reviews the diff <headBefore>..HEAD with read-only tools and flags concerns. Any flag promotes status to 'needs_review'. Adds ~$0.002/agent and ~30-60s per batch.
Mechanisms D + A combined (recommended for production migrations and cross-file refactors). The structured exit catches what the agent admits; the critic catches what the agent omits.

Mechanisms D + A + (future) human-review panel. Today equivalent to 'both' — the modal panel that pauses on findings with diff highlighted is roadmapped for v0.2.1+. Set this when you want the future-ready intent recorded in your settings.
claudeOrchestrator.verification.description: Verification mode applied at the end of wait_for_agents. Default 'structured' applies Mechanism D (structured exit) at zero runtime cost — see research/VERIFICATION_MECHANISMS.md for the full rationale. Set to 'both' for migrations, refactors with assertion contract changes, or anywhere a silent mistake would cost more than the ~$0.002 critic per agent.

scripts.compile: npm run compile:extension && npm run compile:webview
